meta.scope: Mexico batch 12 — Finish CDMX alcaldías pattern (add more key alcaldías) + two poorest/most marginalized states (Chiapas and Guerrero) using State → Metro → Key municipalities → Local institute / judiciary / IMSS / CNGMD / Economic Census structure. Purpose: test homogeneity of statistical infrastructure across rich vs poor Mexico.
meta.homogeneity_note: This batch deliberately contrasts high-capacity metros (CDMX) with the two highest-poverty states (Chiapas 66.0% multidimensional poverty, Guerrero 58.1%) to reveal whether the same statistical hierarchy exists or breaks down in marginalized regions.

candidates.title: Alcaldía Cuauhtémoc — statistical and administrative profile
candidates.description: Central, high-visibility alcaldía (historic center, dense commercial and administrative activity). Profile drawn from CNGMD, census, DENUE, SI CDMX indicators and local administration data.
referenced_by: Censo de Población y Vivienda alcaldía tabulations
Local government performance and budget reporting
candidates.notes: High-profile central alcaldía. Often appears near the top of approval rankings. Dense commercial activity and heavy day-time floating population. Statistical identity is almost entirely supplied by national and city-level systems rather than a strong independent municipal statistical office.

candidates.title: Alcaldía Benito Juárez — statistical and administrative profile
candidates.publisher: Alcaldía Benito Juárez / INEGI / IPDP CDMX
candidates.description: One of the most affluent and statistically visible alcaldías. Frequently ranks as the safest in ENSU perception data and high in service satisfaction. Profile assembled from CNGMD, census, city indicators and local reporting.
candidates.notes: Contrast alcaldía: high income, high service satisfaction, low perceived insecurity. Demonstrates intra-CDMX heterogeneity. Data still primarily national/city systems rather than a robust independent municipal statistical office.

candidates.title: Alcaldía Tláhuac — statistical and administrative profile
candidates.description: Peripheral, lower-income alcaldía that frequently ranks among the highest in perceived insecurity (ENSU). Useful contrast to central/affluent alcaldías.
candidates.notes: Peripheral ‘awkward’ alcaldía inside the capital. High perceived insecurity in ENSU contrasts sharply with Benito Juárez. Shows that even inside CDMX the statistical and lived reality is not homogeneous.

candidates.title: Chiapas (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity
candidates.publisher: INEGI + CEIEG Chiapas + Gobierno de Chiapas
candidates.description: Poorest state by multidimensional poverty (66.0% in 2024) and extreme poverty (27.1%). Parent node for any Chiapas metro or municipal zoom. Statistical capacity exists but is thinner and more dependent on national programmes.
candidates.notes: Highest multidimensional poverty (66.0%) and extreme poverty (27.1%) in 2024 INEGI measurement. Large indigenous population, rural, and historically marginalized. Tests whether the same State → Metro → Municipality → Local institute hierarchy exists under conditions of extreme poverty.

candidates.title: Tuxtla Gutiérrez (capital) — metropolitan / municipal statistical profile
candidates.description: Capital and principal urban centre of Chiapas. Functions as the limited ‘metro’ node for the state. Data come primarily from national series (census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD) with thinner local institutional production than CDMX or Jalisco.
candidates.notes: In the poorest state the ‘metro’ node is essentially the capital city. Local statistical institute (CEIEG) capacity is weaker than IIEG Jalisco or IPDP CDMX; most usable series remain national programmes cut to state or municipality.

candidates.title: Comité Estatal de Información Estadística y Geográfica de Chiapas (CEIEG) / state statistical coordination
candidates.description: State-level statistical coordination body. Produces or compiles poverty, social and geographic information, but with thinner independent publication cadence than IIEG Jalisco or IPDP CDMX.
candidates.notes: Tests homogeneity: in the poorest state the local statistical institute exists but produces fewer original recurring statistical products. Heavy dependence on INEGI national programmes is visible. Poverty reports (e.g. 66% multidimensional poverty) are often compilations of INEGI data rather than independent surveys.

candidates.title: Guerrero (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity
candidates.description: Second-poorest state by multidimensional poverty (58.1% in 2024) and extreme poverty (21.3%). High marginalization, indigenous population, and weak local statistical infrastructure relative to northern or central states.
candidates.notes: Deliberate contrast case. 58.1% multidimensional poverty and 21.3% extreme poverty (2024). Tests whether the State → Metro → Municipality → Local institute hierarchy survives in a high-poverty, high-marginalization environment.

candidates.title: Acapulco de Juárez (and metro) — municipal / metropolitan statistical profile
candidates.description: Principal urban centre and nominal ‘metro’ node for Guerrero. Tourism-dependent, repeatedly hit by hurricanes and insecurity. Data almost entirely from national programmes (census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census) with limited independent local statistical production.
candidates.notes: In a high-poverty state the ‘metro’ node is essentially the main tourist city. Local statistical capacity is thin; most usable series remain national cuts. Hurricane impact and insecurity further complicate continuous local data production.

candidates.title: Poder Judicial / Fiscalía del Estado de Guerrero — statistical presence
candidates.publisher: Poder Judicial del Estado de Guerrero / Fiscalía General del Estado
candidates.description: State justice and prosecution institutions. Data appear mainly through national CNIJE / CNPJE rather than rich independent local yearbooks.
candidates.notes: Tests homogeneity: in a high-poverty, high-insecurity state the local judicial statistical production is thin. Most usable numbers come from the national INEGI justice censuses rather than a robust independent state judicial statistical office.

candidates.title: Chiapas poverty and social-lag reports (CEIEG / Bienestar compilations)
candidates.publisher: CEIEG Chiapas / Secretaría de Bienestar / INEGI
candidates.description: State-level poverty and social-lag compilations. Largely re-workings of INEGI ENIGH and multidimensional poverty results rather than independent primary surveys.
referenced_by: Informe Anual sobre la Situación de Pobreza y Rezago Social
candidates.notes: In the poorest state, local ‘statistical’ products are frequently compilations of INEGI data rather than original primary surveys. Reveals thinner independent statistical capacity.

candidates.title: Acapulco de Juárez — extended municipal profile (tourism, insecurity, recovery)
candidates.publisher: INEGI / Ayuntamiento de Acapulco / Guerrero state sources
candidates.description: Principal urban centre of Guerrero. Tourism-dependent economy repeatedly affected by hurricanes and high insecurity. Statistical presence is almost entirely national programmes (census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census, tourism indicators) with limited independent local statistical production.
candidates.notes: In the second-poorest state the main urban node has thin independent statistical capacity. Hurricane recovery and insecurity further disrupt continuous local data. Most usable numbers remain national cuts. Clear contrast with CDMX alcaldías or Zapopan.

candidates.title: Tuxtla Gutiérrez — extended capital / municipal profile
candidates.description: Capital and principal urban centre of the poorest state. Functions as the limited metro node. Data almost entirely from national programmes with thinner local institutional production.
referenced_by: National census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census
CEIEG compilations of INEGI poverty data
candidates.notes: In the poorest state the capital still relies overwhelmingly on INEGI national programmes. Local CEIEG products are frequently re-compilations rather than original primary surveys. Demonstrates thinner statistical infrastructure.

proposed_edges.basis: Monterrey municipality is the core of the Nuevo León entity and ZMM.
Economic Census provides structural benchmark data that feed national accounts and municipal economic rankings.
